programme.title: Lost Cities With Albert Lin
programme.sub-title: In the footsteps of the Templars
programme.desc: Fans of the adventures of Indiana Jones have the opportunity to see that reality is not inferior to film fiction, and scientists are constantly revising their knowledge about the past.The fabulous treasures of the Templars, the lost gold of El Dorado, the ruins of a city called the Venice of the Pacific, the holy places of the Incas and the mystery of Stonehenge - these are selected points on the map of Albert Lin's documentary journey.The scientist uses advanced technologies and various gadgets to see what was previously hidden from the eyes of archaeologists and historians.The legendary treasure of the order The exciting expedition begins in Acre in Israel - a strategic port city whose history dates back to the Bronze Age.A modern adventurer is looking for traces of the legendary Templar kingdom and its valuables.In the basement of a historic church, he meets Dr. Eliezer Stern, who is his guide to the heritage of brave knights from the 12th and 13th centuries.One can see what a brilliant engineering achievement the crypts equipped with huge water reservoirs were.While looking for gold that the monks obtained from pilgrims, he reaches a tunnel connecting the port with other districts of the city.Thanks to advanced technologies, it creates a map.Will it lead him to the treasure?

programme.title: Nazi Megastructures: Battle Ready
programme.desc: Profiles of engineers responsible for the construction of the most dangerous military facilities.Their works contributed to the technological revolution.The figures of Heinrich Himmler and Joseph Goebbels, who were completely devoted to Hitler, will also be introduced.The Führer assigned them the task of building the Nazi social machine.The program will also discuss the attack on the Soviet Union and the failure of total war tactics.You will be able to learn about the creation of the battleships Bismarck and Tirpitz, as well as the bunkers intended to protect submarines.In addition, the creators will talk about the conflict in the Pacific and the largest floating fortress armed with powerful guns.

programme.title: Genghis Khan: the Secret History of the Mongols
programme.sub-title: Temujin: The boy who became khan
programme.desc: A profile of a man who went down in history as a brilliant military strategist.The six-episode series will present little-known facts from the life of the fearless leader.The authors will show how, after a difficult childhood and captivity, he managed to gain power, unite the quarreling tribes, build an invincible army and subjugate all those who opposed him, including his former allies.Impressive conquests will be discussed, including:expansion into the West, campaigns against the neighboring Tangut people and the Chinese Jin Empire.The troops he commanded were known for the mobility of their cavalry, carrying out rapid attacks and retreats, and applying psychological pressure on their opponents.They used innovative techniques during sieges of even well-fortified cities.Genghis Khan became one of the most important figures in history, expanding his empire to unprecedented sizes.It stretched from the Pacific to the Caspian and Black Seas.The creators of the series are based on a new translation of the anonymous chronicle "The Secret History of the Mongols", which is the oldest known monument of writing of the steppe peoples of Central Asia A fascinating history lesson that combines a story about the past with spectacular stagings like a blockbuster.The six-episode documentary series presents little-known facts from the life of the legendary leader, focusing on his subsequent conquests and centuries-old legacy.The authors based their work on a new translation of the anonymous chronicle "The Secret History of the Mongols", which is the oldest known written monument of the steppe peoples of Central Asia.The experts' statements are the background of a historical thriller in which the realities of the 12th and 13th centuries have been carefully recreated.Thanks to this, the distant past becomes vivid and exciting.A boy from the steppes The starting point of the story about the life of the founder of the Mongol Empire are the turbulent years of his youth.Temujin, later known as Genghis Khan, experienced the decline of his family, poverty and a life of insecurity.He witnessed the tribes fighting.Viewers will see how this survival school influenced his ambitions and character development.As a young warrior, Genghis Khan formed alliances to save his abducted wife, Börte.Thanks to the marriage, he gained the support of the Kereite chief.He consistently made decisions that allowed him to create the largest land empire in history.

Chernobyl: Inside the Meltdown
programme.desc: On April 26, 1986, an explosion destroyed the fourth block of the Chernobyl power plant.The accident was caused by design defects in the reactor and errors during the safety test.It was the worst nuclear disaster in history.The explosion released 400 times more radiation than the bomb dropped on Hiroshima.40 years after the tragedy, its consequences will be shown - from KGB activities to military operations in Ukraine.There will be plenty of witness accounts that will shed new light on the dramatic events.The speakers will include:liquidator working on the roof of reactor 3 and journalist Wyatt Andrews, who was covering the information blockade in Moscow On April 8, the remains of the fourth reactor were still unextinguished.The authorities finally decide to evacuate.50,000 people take supplies for three days.They don't know that they will never return to their homes.Meanwhile, firefighters with burns are being watched by the KGB.Swedish technicians at the Forsmark nuclear power plant are the first to detect increased levels of radiation.They alert the world about the catastrophe that the USSR authorities are trying to hide.Events two weeks after the explosion will be discussed.The authors will explain how attempts were made to hide the truth.

programme.title: Air Crash Investigation 21
programme.desc: Reconstructions of real plane crashes.By recreating the course of events, the program's creators try to understand what led to the unfortunate events.They recreate the circumstances in which the tragedy occurred: the weather, the atmosphere on board the plane, the decisions and actions of the pilots.They also show the work of people investigating the causes of disasters and conduct a computer flight simulation.Viewers can hear various comments from specialists and testimonies of witnesses to these events.The creators of the program will prove that air accidents are often caused by human slowness and lack of imagination.Each disaster is thoroughly analyzed and the lessons learned help minimize the number of tragedies in the future.

programme.title: Iron Curtain: Life Under Soviet Occupation
programme.desc: A story about the Sovietization process, from 1944 to the construction of the Berlin Wall.After World War II, the countries of Central and Eastern Europe found themselves in the Soviet zone.The events that led to such a division of the Old Continent will be presented.Viewers will learn how it affected the everyday lives of citizens of these countries and what forms of resistance they encountered.Experts will explain the mechanisms of Soviet domination.There will be witnesses' accounts, interviews, discussions of scientific works and archives including propaganda films, home recordings and fictional stories.
